feature: A preview ends with a readiness verdict, the recommended command and the remedy of every remaining item; an apply ends with its run state

also: worktree whose only blocker is ignored files
remote branch merged only into the local branch
detached worktree or worktree holding a kept branch

expected: The preview ends with ONE_SHOT (one run of the recommended command reaches the end state), PARTIAL (something remains that no flag lifts) or BLOCKED (a gate fails and nothing can run); the verdict judges the recommended command, not the command as typed.

The end state is only main and <branch> as local branches, the worktrees of the deleted branches removed, and every remote branch deleted or NOT_TOUCHED; it leaves out a worktree the command never touches (a detached one, or one that holds main or another kept branch), and the report lists it.

The recommended command is the /GitSweep <branch> --apply line, with --remote and --lang as given, and exactly the flags that lift something: --discard-ignored with the ignored paths it deletes listed, --push (whether or not it was typed) when a remote branch is PUSH_THEN_DELETE, with the publish prediction; a flag that lifts nothing is never recommended and none is added silently.

Every failed gate is reported at once with its remedy, in /GitConverge and in /GitSweep (a --remote that git remote does not list included), and every blocker, UNKNOWN and PREDICTED_CONFLICT is followed by the action that lifts it.

A PUSH_THEN_DELETE branch kept for want of --push has the remedy rerun with --push (or push <branch> by hand); a PENDING_PUSH branch has the remedy clear the condition the report names (publish the remote default by hand, fetch and merge a newer remote tip, or the rows of an UNKNOWN phase 2).

The apply report ends with the run state COMPLETE or PARTIAL and, for PARTIAL, a Next command: line with the exact line to run after the remedies, carrying --remote and --lang as given and --push when a branch ended PUSH_THEN_DELETE or PENDING_PUSH because the publish was skipped, failed or unconfirmed (not when <branch> is the remote default); the flags of the recommended command and of that line come in the order --apply, --discard-ignored, --push, --remote, --lang, and the line is left out when no rerun would change anything.

contains: ### One-shot readiness
A preview ends with a readiness verdict and a recommended command, and an apply report ends with the run state it reached

- `ONE_SHOT`: no gate fails; every source is `MERGE` or `CONTAINED` and its only delete blocker, if any, is `BLOCKED_IGNORED_FILES`, which `--discard-ignored` lifts; no source is `PREDICTED_CONFLICT`; phase 2 is not `UNKNOWN`; and every remote branch is `SAFE_CANDIDATE`, `PUSH_THEN_DELETE` or `NOT_TOUCHED`.
A worktree the command never touches (a detached one, or one that holds `main` or another kept branch) is not part of the end state; the report lists it.

so the user sees whether one run of the **recommended command** reaches the **end state**: only `main` and `<branch>` remain as local branches, the worktrees of the deleted branches are removed, and every remote branch is deleted or `NOT_TOUCHED`.

with the flags in the order `--apply`, `--discard-ignored`, `--push`, `--remote`, `--lang`; it carries `--push` when `--push` was typed in this run, or some remote branch ended `PUSH_THEN_DELETE` or `PENDING_PUSH` for a reason the user can clear (the publish was skipped, failed or unconfirmed, or the remote tip needs a fetch and merge), and not when the only reason is that `<branch>` is the remote default; when phase 2 is `UNKNOWN` no remote branch is classified, the report shows the phase 2 rows, and `--push` is carried only when it was typed;
The verdict judges the recommended command, not the command as typed
- `PARTIAL`: no gate fails, but something remains that no flag lifts
a `PENDING_PUSH` whose publish step is not predicted to run
- `BLOCKED`: a gate fails, so nothing can run; the report lists every failed gate with its remedy.
A failed gate makes the readiness verdict `BLOCKED`.

**Recommended command.** For `ONE_SHOT` and `PARTIAL`, the full line `/GitSweep <branch> --apply` (with `--remote <name>` and `--lang <language>` as given, and the flags in the order `--apply`, `--discard-ignored`, `--push`, `--remote`, `--lang`)
`--discard-ignored` only when a worktree's only delete blocker is `BLOCKED_IGNORED_FILES`, with every ignored path that it deletes listed next to the line

`--push` only when at least one remote branch is `PUSH_THEN_DELETE` (whether or not `--push` was typed), with the publish prediction (commit count, whether it creates the remote branch) next to the line
A flag that lifts nothing is never recommended, and a flag that discards files or publishes commits is never added silently.

**Run state (apply report).** `COMPLETE` when the end state was reached; otherwise `PARTIAL` with the same remaining items and, as the last line, `Next command:` with the exact line to run once the remedies are done
Readiness: ONE_SHOT / PARTIAL / BLOCKED, recommended command, remaining items + remedies

built by the rules above from the final survey
### Remedies
Every failed gate, delete blocker, `UNKNOWN` status, `PREDICTED_CONFLICT`, and stop of an apply (a conflict, a failed check) in a report is followed by the action that lifts it.
Every gate is evaluated, and the report names every failed gate with its remedy (**Remedies** below), so one run shows everything the user must clear before the next one.
| gate: target is `main` | name the integration branch instead of `main` |
| gate: invoking worktree dirty | commit the changes, or `git stash push --include-untracked`; `git status --short --untracked-files=all` lists what counts |
| `BLOCKED_IGNORED_FILES` | add `--discard-ignored` (the listed files are lost) or move the files out of the worktree |
| `BLOCKED_UPSTREAM_OF_KEPT` | `git branch --unset-upstream <x>` on the branch that tracks it, or retarget that branch |
| `PREDICTED_CONFLICT` | merge that source into the target by hand and resolve it (`git merge refs/heads/<source>`), then rerun; a conflict stops the apply |
| `UNKNOWN` | establish the fact its evidence names; for a case collision, the rename procedure |
A report with a failed gate has no plan: the rest of the preview is not made.
**Remaining items.** For `PARTIAL`, every item that stays: the branch or worktree, its classification, its evidence, its remedy and whether the user must rerun afterwards.
| phase 2 `UNKNOWN`: remote default unknown | `git remote set-head <remote> --auto` |
| phase 2 `UNKNOWN`: no `refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/<remote>/*` mapping | `git config --add remote.<remote>.fetch '+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/<remote>/*'`, then `git fetch <remote>` |
| phase 2 `UNKNOWN`: push URL differs from the fetch URL | make them the same (`git config --unset-all remote.<remote>.pushurl`) or sweep the remote that the push URL names |
| phase 2 `UNKNOWN` or `STALE` after the live check | `git fetch <remote>` (and `git remote set-head <remote> --auto` when the default changed), then rerun |
| gate: `--remote <name>` not listed by `git remote` | name a listed remote (`git remote -v`), or add it with `git remote add <name> <url>` |
| `PUSH_THEN_DELETE` (kept: `--push` not typed) | rerun with `--push`, or `git push <remote> refs/heads/<branch>:refs/heads/<branch>` yourself, then rerun |

| `PENDING_PUSH` | clear the condition the report names, then rerun: if `<branch>` is the remote default, publish it by hand or through your review process (the command never pushes the remote default); if the remote tip is not an ancestor, `git fetch <remote>` and merge it into `<branch>`, then rerun with `--push`; if the push failed or was refused, satisfy the host's rule (branch protection, a hook) and rerun with `--push`, or publish by hand; if phase 2 is `UNKNOWN`, see its rows |

| `PUSH_SKIPPED`, `PUSH_FAILED`, `PUSH_UNCONFIRMED` | clear the named condition: fetch and merge a newer remote tip; satisfy the host's branch protection or hook; fix the failed validation (see the failed-check row); for `<branch>` being `main` or the remote default, publish it by hand or through your review process; or publish by hand, then rerun |
| `KEPT_LOCAL` | clear the local blocker named for that branch |
| `BLOCKED_UPSTREAM` | `git branch --unset-upstream <x>` on the local branch that tracks it |
| `KEPT_NOT_MERGED` | review it and merge it into `<branch>`, or delete it on the host yourself; the command never deletes it |
| `BLOCKED_BAD_NAME` | delete or rename it on the host |

`PENDING_PUSH` marks a branch that no push of this run clears: the publish is not predicted to run (for example `<branch>` is the remote default), or the push was skipped, failed or unconfirmed.
The remedy of the first is to rerun with `--push` or to push `<branch>` by hand; the remedy of the second is to clear the condition the report names.
